baseline: Your fuzz test finishes on the real parser, with no sanitizer report

variants.name: reads-the-length-past-the-end
variants.label: parse() reads the length byte even when the message ends right after the magic byte
variants.hint: A message that is CUT OFF can end in the middle of a packet header. Try every prefix of valid messages, and give parse() an exactly sized buffer.

variants.name: reads-the-payload-past-the-end
variants.label: parse() trusts the length byte and reads a payload that is longer than the message
variants.hint: Inputs whose length byte promises more bytes than there are. Random bytes find this one; so does cutting valid messages short.

variants.name: reads-the-checksum-past-the-end
variants.label: parse() reads the checksum one byte past the end when only the checksum is missing
variants.hint: A valid message with its LAST byte removed. Try every prefix of valid messages.

variants.name: rejects-long-payloads
variants.label: parse() rejects every payload of 128 bytes or more
variants.hint: Valid messages with long payloads (the length byte at the top of its range) must round-trip. Random bytes will not find this one.

variants.name: hangs-on-an-empty-packet
variants.label: parse() never finishes when it meets a packet with an empty payload (A5 00 00)
variants.hint: Random bytes almost never contain A5 00 00. Build valid messages with make_packet, including EMPTY payloads.

variants.name: drops-a-last-empty-packet
variants.label: parse() silently loses an empty packet at the end of the message
variants.hint: This bug never crashes: only a PROPERTY finds it. Encode payloads, parse them back and compare. Include an empty payload.
